questions.stem: A man starts facing North, turns 90° clockwise, then 180° anticlockwise. Which direction is he now facing?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Start: North. Turn 90° clockwise (right): faces East. Turn 180° anticlockwise from East: 180° anticlockwise = turn to face the opposite direction = West. Final facing: West.

questions.stem: Ravi walks 5 km North, then 3 km East, then 5 km South. How far is he from his starting point and in which direction?
questions.explanation: B is correct. 5 km North, then 5 km South cancel each other (net N-S = 0). 3 km East remains. Distance from start = 3 km, direction = East. No Pythagoras needed when N-S cancels completely.

questions.stem: A boy walks 4 km West, then 3 km South. What is the straight-line distance from his starting point?
questions.explanation: A is correct. The path creates a right angle (West then South). The straight-line distance is the hypotenuse: √(4²+3²) = √25 = 5 km. This is the classic 3-4-5 right triangle.

questions.stem: Seema is facing South-East. She turns 135° anticlockwise. Which direction is she now facing?
questions.explanation: A is correct. Compass positions: N=0°, NE=45°, E=90°, SE=135°, S=180°, SW=225°, W=270°, NW=315°. SE is at 135° from North. Turning 135° anticlockwise (CCW): 135° − 135° = 0° = North. Final direction: North.

questions.stem: Kiran starts at point A, walks 6 km North to B, then 8 km East to C. What is the shortest distance from A to C?
questions.explanation: A is correct. 6 km North then 8 km East forms a right angle at B. AC = √(AB²+BC²) = √(6²+8²) = √(36+64) = √100 = 10 km. This is the 6-8-10 Pythagorean triple (= 3-4-5 × 2).

questions.stem: A person is standing at a point facing West. He turns 90° clockwise, then 45° anticlockwise, then 45° clockwise. In which direction is he facing now?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Start: West. Turn 90° CW: West→North. Turn 45° ACW: North→NW. Turn 45° CW: NW→North. Final direction: North. The last two turns (45° ACW then 45° CW) cancel each other out.

questions.stem: Neeta walks 3 km towards East, then 2 km towards North, then 5 km towards West, then 2 km towards South. How far and in which direction is she from the starting point?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Net East-West: 3 East − 5 West = −2 = 2 km West. Net North-South: 2 North − 2 South = 0. She is exactly 2 km West of her starting point.

questions.stem: If the shadow of a person falls to his right side, in which direction is he facing?
questions.explanation: C is correct. In the morning, the sun is in the East. Shadow falls opposite to the sun. If the shadow falls to the RIGHT, the sun is to the LEFT. When facing South, East is to your LEFT → shadow falls West, which is to your RIGHT. So the person is facing SOUTH. (In afternoon with sun in West, the person would face North.)

questions.stem: Town X is to the East of Town Y. Town Z is to the North of Town X. Town W is to the South of Town Y. If you travel from W to Z, which direction do you generally travel?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Plotting positions: Y is reference. X is East of Y. Z is North of X → Z is NE of Y. W is South of Y → SW relative to Z. Traveling from W (south of Y) to Z (north of X = NE of Y) requires going North-East.

questions.stem: Vikram walks 10 km North, 6 km East, 10 km South, and then 3 km West. How far is he from his starting point?
questions.explanation: B is correct. N-S: 10 North − 10 South = 0 (cancel). E-W: 6 East − 3 West = 3 km East. He is 3 km East of starting point. No Pythagoras needed when one axis cancels.
